<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/permission-metadata.mdx`  _(via default_off (literal, a string literal in MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponseSchema), default_on (literal, a string literal in MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponseSchema))_
- `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx`  _(via default_on (literal, a string literal in MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponseSchema))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json db357f6da9f787ff6285c20c70bc02a1bc138d35` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4f8bfa838c2c52683fdd9e0aa3843743adb6775f` — the merge of head `e51961f0ab8b123546f06a079c94829219dbb216` into base `db357f6da9f787ff6285c20c70bc02a1bc138d35`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4f8bfa838c2c52683fdd9e0aa3843743adb6775f && git checkout 4f8bfa838c2c52683fdd9e0aa3843743adb6775f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin db357f6da9f787ff6285c20c70bc02a1bc138d35 e51961f0ab8b123546f06a079c94829219dbb216 && git checkout -B drift-repro db357f6da9f787ff6285c20c70bc02a1bc138d35 && git merge --no-ff e51961f0ab8b123546f06a079c94829219dbb216

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json db357f6da9f787ff6285c20c70bc02a1bc138d35
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs db357f6da9f787ff6285c20c70bc02a1bc138d35` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `567e3dc8230bd5af5d160a005efee9cecb831964`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts, skills/objectstack-api/references/_index.md + packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints-has-any-queue.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/ownership-queue-service.ts, packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-references.ts, packages/spec/scripts/lib/skill-map-guards.ts, packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, .changeset/28508-me-permissions-response-contract.md, packages/verify/src/me-permissions-has-any-queue.test.ts, and the ui reader `ui/packages/permissions/src/MePermissionsProvider.tsx` (objectui), read against card #28508 (ruling record 6557794880, server-half landing 3944d2e1, os-dev-report 6559267240) and consumer card #28428.

Check-runs on the head at review time (42): `Check Changeset` completed **failure** (step "Guard against accidental major bumps (launch window)", verdict `none-baseline-moved`); `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Spec property liveness`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Auto Label`, `filter` completed success; `Test Core (1..8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`, every `Type Check ·` and every other `Lint ·` job still **in_progress**; the rest skipped. So the derived gate families are not yet answered by CI; the dev's 115/115 local gate record is the dev's account, not a gate verdict, and the one completed gate that reads the declarations is red.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named:

1. **`@objectstack/spec/api` gains six exports** — `MePermissionsAnonymousResponseSchema`, `MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponseSchema`, `MePermissionsResponseSchema` and their three `z.input` types (`api/index.ts` already `export *`s `auth.zod`). Right: api-surface, export-origins, declaration-map (6 each) and json-schema manifest (3 schema ids) all carry exactly these and nothing else; `content/docs/references/api/auth.mdx` and `index.mdx` (1584 to 1587, API 460 to 463) are the generator's output of the same.
2. **The schema matches every body the live route answers.** Read in `current-user-endpoints.ts` on the head: anonymous `{ authenticated: false }` (bare literal, line ~900) is exactly the strict anonymous branch; the degraded literal (no resolver or no metadata, ~line 940) sends `authenticated, userId, tenantId (?? null), positions, permissionSets, objects: {}, fields: {}, hasAnyQueue` with `systemPermissions`/`tabPermissions` absent — the two optional keys, every other key required: matches; the full body and the outer-catch closed body both go through `mePermissionsBody`, now return-typed `MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponse`, with all eleven keys. `positions` from `execCtx.positions` (`z.array(z.string()).default([])`), `permissionSets` from `execCtx.permissions` (same) or `resolved.map(name).filter(Boolean)`, `fields` from `buildEffectiveFieldPermissions` whose return type is exactly `Record of { readable: boolean; editable: boolean }` (strict entry holds), `tabPermissions` merged only from the four-value `tabRank` vocabulary (the enum holds), `objects` from `buildEffectiveObjectPermissions` whose entries are `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema`. Right. **The schema is bound, not declaration-only:** tsc pins the two `mePermissionsBody` bodies to the type; the route test's `read()` and the verify door test parse every provoked body (full, degraded, closed, anonymous, service absent / method absent / throwing) through `MePermissionsResponseSchema` with `issues == []`. The degraded and anonymous literals are bound only by those tests (the dev's `check:route-envelope` reason for keeping them bare is read in the file's own comment and is accepted).
3. **`objects` entries stay tolerant.** `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema` is `.strip()` by design (wire-side tolerance, #4001) wrapped in `acceptRetiredDefaultResidue`. So "an unknown sibling is refused" is true at the top level and in a `fields` entry, and NOT inside an `objects` entry (dropped silently). The dev disclosed it; the card's Acceptance 1 names the sibling of `hasAnyQueue`, which is top-level. Right as scoped, recorded as a limit of the contract, not a defect.
4. **`IOwnershipQueueService` gains a REQUIRED member `hasAnyQueue(organizationId)`.** This is a public-surface change to a published `contracts/` interface that out-of-tree code implements (the module's own header: "a host registered under the name"). It is a widening for callers and a compile-time break for implementers. Judged wrong as declared — see ② and ④.
5. **`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json` gains 11 keys** (`api/MePermissions*Response:*`). Right as generated output; but a moved authorable-surface shard IS the baseline `check-changeset-no-major` reads for the level axis, and the PR declares `Metadata-protocol: none`. See ②.
6. **Strictness ledger 474 to 477**: three new strict sites (anonymous object, authenticated object, the `fields` entry). Right.
7. **`variant-docs.json`** gains `authenticated:false|true` as `not-authorable`. Right: a wire discriminator, nobody authors it.
8. **ADR-0122 pins 808 to 811** as `Iso_` (not `Parsed`): right only if the three schemas are isomorphic; the pin is tsc-checked, and the authenticated branch nests `EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema` (a pipe over a strict-extended-then-stripped object). The dev's typecheck is the only reading; CI `Type Check` is in progress. Accepted provisionally on the pin's own mechanism.
9. **`@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`**: `AnyQueueReader` becomes a `Pick` of the contract's `hasAnyQueue`, read as `Partial` through the locator with the `typeof` guard kept, and `mePermissionsBody` is return-typed. Wire byte-identical (no key added, removed or re-ordered). Right.
10. **`@objectstack/plugin-sharing`**: docblock only. Right; `OwnershipQueueService.hasAnyQueue` already landed in 3944d2e1 (line 222 on main) and matches the contract's docblock claim ("true exactly when some name would resolve through resolveQueue": active declared queues, else authored names not under a declared name).
11. **`skills/objectstack-api/references/_index.md`**: 22 new "Transitive dependencies" pointers and no new core entry. Right as generated: the new `import { EffectiveObjectPermissionSchema } from '../security/permission.zod'` in a core file of the `objectstack-api` skill pulls `security/permission.zod.ts` and its closure (data/field, data/object, ui/view, ui/chart, ui/bulk-action, automation …) into the index. Accurate, but see ④.
12. **Changeset**: `patch` × 3 with `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Wrong — see ②.

### ② Semver level

**Must-fix (gate-red).** `Check Changeset` on this head FAILS with `none-baseline-moved`: the PR declares `Clause-②: yes` with no arm and `Metadata-protocol: none`, and moves `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`. The workflow's own rule (pr-automation.yml "WHICH LEVEL", maintainer ruling A 2026-10-21): a declared `none` "may not move a `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` shard (`none-baseline-moved`, exit 1)", and "a baseline is never edited to quiet this gate". The PR body's reading ("the manifest lists every schema key per subpath, not because the keys are authorable") is exactly the reading the gate refuses by name. Precedent on `main` for the same shape — a new request/response schema in `api/` that moved this shard — is uniform: #28440 (9b1dc992c), #28447 (462935db8), #28595 (519089e17), #27232 (8bb2c31bd), #27063 (f9f27a06f) all shipped `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`. The card's own text says `Clause-②: yes (a response contract widens)`. Required: in the PR body AND the changeset, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, and `@objectstack/spec` graded `minor` (the gate needs at least one moved package at `minor`; `plugin-hono-server` and `plugin-sharing` may stay `patch`). Not the reverse: no edit to the shard. The gate re-reads the body on `edited`, but the changeset file needs a push.

**Must-fix (declaration).** The required `hasAnyQueue` member on the published `IOwnershipQueueService` is a break for every out-of-tree implementer (`class X implements IOwnershipQueueService` stops compiling), shipped under `patch` with no `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition. AGENTS.md: "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING"; ADR-0087 D7 treats a published runtime interface as compiler-carried and counts "a member added … re-typed or made optional" as a surface change. The repo's practice for a member added to a published contract is OPTIONAL: `declaredQueueNamed?` on this very interface (a9f654ebf, ADR-0142) and `getRecordFieldAccess?` on `ISecurityService` (f9f27a06f, `yes (widening)`). The route itself still guards `typeof hasAnyQueue !== 'function'` — the only consumer treats the member as optional, so the contract as written and the code that reads it disagree. Two honest shapes: (a) `hasAnyQueue?(…)` optional, mirroring `declaredQueueNamed?`, with the docblock saying a service without it answers `false` at the carrier (the route already does); or (b) keep it required and declare the break — `(narrowing)` arm, BREAKING banner, ADR-0087 disposition, migration line ("add `hasAnyQueue(organizationId)`; return `false` to keep today's wire"). Reviewer's recommendation is (a): the ruling record asked for the method on the contract and the route reading it through the contract, which (a) satisfies with `Pick`/`Partial` exactly as the head already compiles, and it leaves the PR a pure widening that then declares `yes (widening)` consistently with the first must-fix.

`skip-changeset` is not in question (three released packages move). With both fixes the level is `@objectstack/spec: minor`, the two plugins `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: added`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0]** "is a required (not optional) hasAnyQueue acceptable as Clause-② yes with no (narrowing) arm, given the only implementer is in-tree?" — **No.** The interface is published for the out-of-tree case; "only implementer is in-tree" is a fact about today's tree, not about the contract. Answered as must-fix in ②, resolution (a) recommended.
- **Deviation 1 / out_of_scope_findings (no `@objectstack/client` method; the route sits in no route ledger).** Verified: `client-url-conformance.test.ts` unions five ledgers (runtime, rest, storage, i18n, auth); `auth-route-ledger.ts` enumerates better-auth routes and `/auth/me/permissions` is `objectstack`-mounted by plugin-hono-server, not better-auth; runtime's ledger has only the `* /auth/**` sdk row (line 623). So a typed client method is refused by design today. Card Target 4 says "The console reads it from the typed client" — this PR meets the declaration half and NOT the typed-client half. **Gap to file** (should-fix, follow-up card, server lane): add `GET /auth/me/permissions` (and `/auth/me/localization`, `/me/apps`, the same supply) to a route ledger so `@objectstack/client` can carry `auth.mePermissions()` under conformance. Until then #28428 types its fetch with `MePermissionsResponse` from `@objectstack/spec/api`, which is workable.
- **Deviation 2** (required member) — answered above.
- **Deviation 3** (`objects` entries keep tolerance) — accepted as a disclosed limit (① item 3).
- **Deviation 4** (`Iso_` pins) — accepted on the pin's mechanism (① item 8).
- **Deviation 5** (no labels) — not reviewed here.
- **Metadata-protocol `none` "by reading"** — refused by the gate on the head; answered in ②.
- **Ablation B not measured** — accepted: A (strictness) and C (route sends an undeclared key: 7/9 route cases and 5/5 door cases red) are the two readings that matter for "bound, not declaration-only"; the `gen:schema` baseline refusing a key rename is itself evidence the key is governed.
- **Dev flag "wire byte-for-byte unchanged"** — holds on reading (① item 9).
- **No escalation needed**: nothing here needs the maintainer; both must-fixes have a mechanical resolution inside the dev's own lane.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts`** — judged against ruling record 6557794880 ("a strict response schema for the `/auth/me/permissions` body (anonymous, degraded, and full/closed shapes, `hasAnyQueue: boolean` declared)") and its first consumer, the route plus the #28428 console.
- Holds against the route: every key, every type, the optional pair's absent-vs-empty distinction, and the discriminator (① item 2). The design choice to make absent `systemPermissions` a declared state ("unknown, fail open") rather than defaulting it is right: a `.default([])` would have turned the degraded body into the closed one on parse, which is the exact conflation #23047 forbids, and it is why the schema is isomorphic and the types are `z.input`.
- Tried to break it: (i) the closed body is `tenantId: identity.tenantId` where `identity.tenantId = execCtx.tenantId ?? null` — nullable holds; (ii) `userId` is `execCtx.userId` guarded truthy — `z.string()` holds; (iii) a `tabPermissions` value outside the four cannot reach the wire (`tabRank` filter) — enum holds; (iv) an `objects` entry carrying `allowRestore: true` would be REFUSED by `acceptRetiredDefaultResidue` while `allowRestore: false` is stripped — `buildEffectiveObjectPermissions` emits only `GRANT_BITS` plus `viewAllRecords`/`modifyAllRecords`/`apiOperations`, never the retired pair, so no live body trips it; (v) the ui reader (`MePermissionsProvider.tsx`) declares `roles: string[]`, `userId: string | null`, `authenticated: boolean` and reads `data?.roles ?? []` — the route has sent `positions`, not `roles`, since ADR-0068, so the ui's hand-written interface was already drifted; this PR does not break it (the ui does not compile against the spec type), but the drift is the very reason the card asked for a declared contract. **Should-fix (follow-up on #28428, ui lane):** the console reads the typed `MePermissionsResponse` from `@objectstack/spec/api` and drops its own `MePermissionsResponse` interface (same name, different shape — a name collision waiting for the import); note `roles` is dead on the wire.
- **Should-fix (note in the schema, no code change required to pass):** `GetEffectivePermissionsResponseSchema` in `api/protocol.zod.ts` (non-strict, `objects` + `systemPermissions` only, backing an unimplemented optional protocol method) is now a second, weaker declaration of the same concept. The new schema's docblock should name it and say which one the wire is, or a later reader will "unify" them the wrong way. The dev noted it in the server-half report; it is not yet written down in the spec.
- The `hasAnyQueue` description is complete and correct against the implementation (declared-and-active OR authored row not shadowed by a declared name; false with no service; false on the closed body) and against the card's non-disclosure rule (no names, no counts) — the route test "the value on the wire is a boolean and nothing else" pins it.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts`** — judged against the ruling record and the implementation on `main` (plugin-sharing line 222).
- The docblock's semantics are exactly the implementation's; the cross-reference to the carrier schema is right. `organizationId: string | null` matches the sibling methods.
- **Must-fix**: required vs optional, as ② states. The interface header promises "every queue-dependent ADMISSION fails closed when the service is not registered"; this member is not an admission, and the route's own comment says an older implementation "answers false" — that is the semantics of an optional member, and the contract should say what the code does. If the maintainer prefers required, the break must be declared, not shipped as `patch` with no arm.

**`skills/objectstack-api/references/_index.md`** — judged against the generator (`build-skill-references.ts`, `skill-map-guards.ts`) and the skill it serves on `main`. The file is generated and in sync (the dev ran `check:skill-refs` green; CI's docs lint is in progress). The content is accurate. **Should-fix:** the one new import drags 22 transitive pointers into the API skill's index, most of them another skill's whole subject (`ui/view.zod.ts`, `ui/chart.zod.ts`, `ui/bulk-action.zod.ts`, `shared/conditional-formatting.zod.ts`, `data/validation.zod.ts` …). The repo already has the instrument for exactly this — `TRANSITIVE_ALLOWLIST` in `skill-map-guards.ts`, whose `objectstack-platform` entry exists because "everything else the closure reaches here is … a different skill's whole subject". An `objectstack-api` row that keeps `security/permission.zod.ts` (the one file an agent reading `MePermissionsAuthenticatedResponse.objects` must follow) and prunes the rest keeps the index a set of pointers an agent can use, which is the generator's own stated standard ("pointing at a schema the body cannot help with sends an agent into node_modules for a lesson that does not exist"). Not a FAIL on its own: the index is true, just bloated.

**Summary of findings.** Must-fix: (1) changeset/declaration level — `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`, as the red `Check Changeset` gate and five precedents require; (2) `hasAnyQueue` required on a published contract is an undeclared implementer break — make it optional like `declaredQueueNamed?` (recommended) or declare the `(narrowing)` break with its carriers. Should-fix: route-ledger gap for a typed client method (file it); #28428 reads the spec type and retires the ui's drifted `MePermissionsResponse` (`roles`); cross-reference `GetEffectivePermissionsResponseSchema` from the new schema; an `objectstack-api` transitive allowlist to prune the 22 new skill pointers.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-7xha1v`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5kE5BrPUPNMMyv6oCH`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0eb64410bfc2f25acf1f9b8985675654342f89ff`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ownership-queue-service.ts, skills/objectstack-api/references/_index.md + .changeset/28508-me-permissions-response-contract.md, packages/spec/scripts/lib/skill-map-guards.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, ui/packages/permissions/src/MePermissionsProvider.tsx, ui/packages/permissions/src/index.ts, ui/packages/permissions/src/PermissionContext.ts, ui/packages/permissions/src/usePermissions.ts, ui/apps/console/src/components/studioEntry.ts, ui/scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs, the 121 ui test files the round-2 diff migrates (`git diff 567e3dc8 0eb64410`), skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md, read against the base record (PR comment 6559372294 on `567e3dc8`), the live PR body, claim amendment 6560444824 and card #28508.

**Delta record.** Round 2 is two commits over the base head (`d86253262`, `0eb64410b`): 129 files, +591/−469, of which 8 are source and 121 are ui test fixtures. Everything the base record judged and does not name below stands unchanged on this head (the schema, its binding to the route and door tests, the wire, the generated artifacts, the plugin-sharing docblock, the verify test): none of those files moved between the two heads.

Check-runs on `0eb64410` at read time (46): `Check Changeset` ran twice — the first run (job 124902013218, started 16:07:30Z on the `synchronize` event) completed **failure** with the SAME `none-baseline-moved` refusal as the base head, because it read the PR body as it stood before the seat's 16:08Z edit (`Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`); the second run (job 124902297495, started 16:08:34Z on the `edited` event, the body now `yes (widening)` / `added`) completed **success** on every step, "Guard against accidental major bumps" included. The gate re-reads the body on `edited` by design, so the newer run is the gate's verdict on this head. Also completed success: `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Flag docs affected`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. Still **in_progress**: `Test Core (1..8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Live E2E UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`. The ui typecheck, `check:spec-symbols` (ci.yml line 3599) and the ui suites are therefore CI's still; the dev's readings (13 packages 0 errors, 1761/1761, 115/115 gates) are the dev's account.

### ① Derived judgments

Delta over the base record's twelve items:

- **Item 4 (contract member), re-judged right.** `hasAnyQueue?(organizationId: string | null): Promise of boolean` is now OPTIONAL on `IOwnershipQueueService`, with a docblock naming `declaredQueueNamed` as its precedent and the route's `false` for an implementation without it.
